source: sars-guide:PAYE-GEN-01-G21 Rev 1 p. 28 (non-standard employment, at least 5 hours per day, earns less than R394 that day: no employees tax)
notes: Casual daily-paid worker, 5 hours a day at R390 a day for 18 days = R7 020 a month: 90 hours a month is about 20.8 hours a week (under 22), no written declaration, so not standard by limb 1; at least 5 hours a day and under R394 a day, so no employees' tax (G21 p. 28, summary table row 3). Under the two-limb reading below, this worker is deemed standard by limb 2 (5+ hours a day and under R394 a day), so row 3 and limb 2 describe the same band: tables apply and, under the threshold, give nil. The tables also give nil (R84 240 a year is under the R99 000 threshold), so this passes today; it guards TS-b against taxing the exempt band at a flat 25% (R1 755.00). NAMED LIMIT found in review: this exempt band cannot be made to differ from the tables. At under 22 hours a week (about 95 hours a month, at most 19 days of 5 hours) and under R394 a day, pay is at most about R7 470 a month (R89 600 a year), always under the R99 000 threshold, so the tables give nil too. Row 3 is therefore a guard, not a gap. G21 p. 28 reading used by all the ts-* cases: the deemed-standard bullet has two limbs, (1) under 22 hours a week with a written declaration of no other employer, and (2) at least 5 hours a day and paid under R394 a day, read as an alternative route to deemed standard; the summary-table rows for non-standard employment follow from that (row 5, under 5 hours a day and under R394, is the residual non-standard case taxed at 25%, not a misprint). TS-b must wire taxStatus and the hours into runCase (oracle.ts hard-codes employmentType permanent and passes no taxStatus or unmodelled input today, so this case cannot see them); once wired, this guard must go red if the status is ignored.
